short_description: Consumer-facing physical trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to gluteofemoral adipose-volume tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing body-distribution trait with workable raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited gluteofemoral fat-distribution tendency and current measured body shape for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with gluteofemoral adipose-volume tendency, meaning a relative tendency toward fat distribution around the hips and upper thighs after adjustment in the source score for BMI and height, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Gluteofemoral adipose-volume tendency is presented here as a cautious panel-relative body-distribution signal, not as a direct body scan, tape measurement, or statement about current appearance. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct body-composition scan, or health advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Real-world fat distribution depends strongly on sex, age, hormones, diet, physical activity, medication use, illness, and other non-modeled factors, so this should not be treated as a precise estimate of current body shape.
The source score is adjusted for BMI and height, so this trait is best read as a relative body-fat-distribution signal rather than as a direct measure of total adiposity or body size.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
